title: The Voicemail (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist family memory
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I leave voicemails that begin with "it's me" as if you know
As if you've been waiting specifically for this show
Then I say my name and then I say it again
And then I say "anyway" which is where things begin to bend

[Pre-Chorus]
My son once played back a voicemail I left for a repairman
Twelve seconds of breathing and then "the tap" — I am that man

[Chorus]
The voicemail knows something I don't know
It knows that what you say and what you mean are quite a show
The voicemail captures everything you thought you'd throw away
The pause before the sentence and the sentence in decay
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
Nobody listens to voicemails anymore — this is known
They'll see the missed call and ring you back on their own
But I keep leaving them for reasons I can't fully say
Maybe so my voice exists somewhere at the end of the day

[Bridge]
There's a voicemail on my mother's phone from nineteen ninety-four
That she said she couldn't delete and I understand that more
Now that my own father's voice exists in no known place
Except the middle of the chest, approximately, in the space

[Outro]
Voicemail knows… the voice outlasts the call… voicemail knows
That's my boy
